concepts.name: tax-sale sequence
concepts.durableOutcome: Explain why a municipality can sell property and reconstruct the statutory sequence.
concepts.definition: The statutory collection path from arrears and lien through notices, title work, advertisement and public sale.
concepts.reason: A bidder enters only at the last stage and needs to understand the rights and work that precede the event.
concepts.mechanism: Unpaid taxes form a priority lien; statutory timing, notice, title search and public-sale requirements move the account toward auction or tender.
concepts.concreteCase: One Inverness parcel called at Port Hood after municipal notice and advertisement.
concepts.problemBeforeName: The listener sees an auction but cannot explain why the municipality may sell another person's land.

analogy.name: runway before takeoff
analogy.relationship: The public event is possible only after required earlier stages.
correspondence: notice and title work are runway checks
the auction is takeoff rather than the whole journey
analogy.limit: A legal sale is not optional pilot judgment; the analogy does not describe owner rights or exact statutory compliance.

concepts.boundary: A tax sale is not a municipal warranty, foreclosure auction or ordinary listing.
concepts.misconception: The auction itself creates the municipality's authority.
concepts.expectedAbility: Put lien, preliminary notice, title search, notice of intent, advertisement and sale in order.

retrievals.freshSituation: A parcel is withdrawn minutes before bidding.
retrievals.listenerTask: Explain which earlier process remains live and why payment can stop the sale.

concepts.name: notice identifiers
concepts.durableOutcome: Distinguish AAN, PID, civic address, assessment, parcel map, legal description, survey and parcel register.
concepts.definition: A set of identifiers and records that answer different questions about tax account, parcel, location, value basis, description, boundary and title.
concepts.reason: Collapsing them into one imagined property is the fastest route to researching the wrong thing.
concepts.mechanism: The notice routes the researcher from AAN and PID to assessment, mapping, registry documents, legal description and professional interpretation.
concepts.concreteCase: An Inverness summary row disagrees with its detail sheet while a civic address points near a building whose PID and deed define the actual land extent.
concepts.problemBeforeName: The auction row shows several numbers and the listener assumes they all mean the same property object.

analogy.name: library catalogue
analogy.relationship: Different identifiers lead to different authoritative records.
correspondence: PID resembles the catalogue key for the parcel
the deed and register resemble the source material reached through the key
analogy.limit: Land records create and evidence legal interests; they are not merely descriptions of a book already understood.

concepts.boundary: A PID map is not a survey and an AAN is not title.
concepts.misconception: The civic address or assessed-owner name proves exactly what land and building are sold.
concepts.expectedAbility: Say which source answers account, parcel, boundary, title and assessment questions.

retrievals.freshSituation: The parcel map and civic-address point disagree.
retrievals.listenerTask: Choose which records to inspect rather than deciding from the map.
retrievals.answerPlacement: At the start of the parcel-biography build.

concepts.name: redemption clock
concepts.durableOutcome: Translate auction, tender, minimum bid, immediate deed, redemption, certificate of sale and tax deed into consequences.
concepts.definition: The six-month statutory period in which qualifying owners or interest holders may recover property sold for taxes, except in the older-arrears case.
concepts.reason: It changes what the bidder receives, can do, must protect and may ultimately keep.
concepts.mechanism: Full payment creates a registered certificate; qualifying redemption payment ends the purchaser's rights, while expiry without redemption permits deed request.
concepts.concreteCase: A building is insured and protected for four months before its owner redeems.
concepts.problemBeforeName: The bidder wins but cannot yet explain whether final title exists or what happens if the owner pays.

analogy.name: forked railway
analogy.relationship: One paid bid can continue toward either discharge or deed.
correspondence: the certificate is the shared track after sale
redemption and deed are different endpoints
analogy.limit: The branches are controlled by law and payment, not by the purchaser choosing a destination.

concepts.boundary: Immediate deed removes the statutory redemption period; it does not promise immediate possession, insurance or usability.
concepts.misconception: Winning at auction always means immediate unrestricted ownership.
concepts.expectedAbility: Narrate certificate, redemption/discharge and deed paths and the older-arrears exception.

retrievals.freshSituation: The treasurer asks for the purchaser's approved repair statement before redemption.
retrievals.listenerTask: Explain why the certificate period required documentation.

concepts.name: evidence classification
concepts.durableOutcome: Explain what a municipal packet already provides, what additional research can responsibly contribute and where professional authority begins.
concepts.definition: A source-traceable record separating reused municipal facts, added research, facts needing a named professional, unresolved uncertainties and conditions that stop a decision.
concepts.reason: Inverness already supplies strong orientation material, while a tax sale still prevents ordinary inspection and leaves legal, physical and decision questions open.
concepts.mechanism: Every research question records whether the fact came from the municipal packet or a new source, plus locator, date, confidence, next authority and decision consequence.
concepts.concreteCase: The municipal packet shows a parcel beside a road, while the added file labels legal access as unresolved for lawyer/surveyor review rather than treating the image as proof.
concepts.problemBeforeName: The researcher has a substantial municipal packet and more screenshots but cannot yet state what was added, what is proved or what remains outside the researcher's role.

analogy.name: four labelled trays
analogy.relationship: Evidence moves into a decision category rather than one undifferentiated pile.
correspondence: verified facts enter the ready tray
disqualifying unknowns enter the stop tray
analogy.limit: Real findings can move between trays as evidence changes; the categories do not calculate legal risk automatically.

concepts.boundary: An unresolved fact is not automatically priceable.
concepts.misconception: Enough online searching turns every uncertainty into a known fact.
concepts.expectedAbility: Classify a finding and name the source or professional needed next.

retrievals.freshSituation: No septic record appears for an old property.
retrievals.listenerTask: Classify the negative search without calling the system compliant.

concepts.name: mapped intersection
concepts.durableOutcome: Build a lawful pre-bid evidence file without entering private property.
concepts.definition: A result saying that the current geometry from one mapped service crosses the selected parcel polygon.
concepts.reason: Visual proximity is easy to overread, while even an exact geometry result inherits the source service’s scale, currency, coverage and legal limits.
concepts.mechanism: The app sends the selected PID geometry and a named service layer through an intersection query, then reports matched mapped features or an honest empty/error state.
concepts.concreteCase: For PID 50308311, the captured build returns River Denys water features and no mapped road/trail intersection, creating separate water and access questions.
concepts.problemBeforeName: The listener sees a line near a parcel and needs language more precise than “there is a road” or “there is water.”
realWorldApplications: NS Marks The Spot parcel inspector

analogy.name: transparent sheets over one outline
analogy.relationship: Each sheet answers only whether its own marks overlap the parcel outline.
correspondence: one sheet represents one layer
overlap creates a question for that layer’s source
analogy.limit: The sheets do not create legal access, survey accuracy, physical condition or complete real-world coverage.

concepts.boundary: A mapped intersection is not a survey, title opinion, legal right-of-way, wetland delineation, flood opinion, inspection or development approval.
concepts.misconception: A visible or returned overlap proves the real-world feature and its legal consequence; an empty result proves absence.
concepts.expectedAbility: State the layer, returned result, retrieval date, limitation and next authoritative question for one parcel.

chapterUses.function: challenge with physical and environmental records

retrievals.freshSituation: A driveway-like line appears beside a parcel but the map reports no road/trail intersection.
retrievals.listenerTask: Write a bounded observation and choose the legal-access records and professionals needed next.
retrievals.answerPlacement: At the start of the landlocked-sliver case.

concepts.name: legal access
concepts.durableOutcome: Test legal access, intended use, zoning, services, boundaries and municipal compliance separately.
concepts.definition: A legally supportable right for the parcel or owner to reach the land, distinct from visual proximity or historic informal use.
concepts.reason: Land without usable legal access can fail a building, financing, service or resale plan despite looking reachable.
concepts.mechanism: Title documents, plans, easements/rights-of-way, public-road frontage and municipal rules are reconciled by appropriate professionals.
concepts.concreteCase: A visible driveway crosses a neighbour's parcel without a confirmed registered right.
concepts.problemBeforeName: The listener can see a route on imagery and assumes that seeing is owning a route.

analogy.name: door and key
analogy.relationship: Physical entry and legal authority to enter are different requirements.
correspondence: the visible driveway is the door
the registered right or frontage evidence is the key
analogy.limit: A right-of-way has detailed scope and obligations; it is not a simple universal key.

concepts.boundary: Legal access does not by itself prove a building permit, servicing or year-round physical suitability.
concepts.misconception: A parcel touching a mapped road has adequate legal and development access.
concepts.expectedAbility: Ask separately about title access, frontage, physical route and intended-use requirements.

retrievals.freshSituation: The tax deed preserves an easement burden.
retrievals.listenerTask: Explain why free-of-encumbrances language did not erase every access relationship.

concepts.name: record limitation
concepts.durableOutcome: Recognize physical and environmental unknowns that records can reveal, narrow or fail to answer.
concepts.definition: The stated boundary on what a database, map, inspection opportunity or missing record can support.
concepts.reason: Tax-sale research is vulnerable to converting a negative search into invented reassurance.
concepts.mechanism: Each result is paired with coverage date, scale, geolocation quality, completeness warning and property-specific next step.
concepts.concreteCase: An abandoned-mine database has no point on the parcel but expressly admits undocumented openings and omitted subsidence.
concepts.problemBeforeName: A clean search screen feels like evidence that nothing is wrong.

analogy.name: flashlight in a dark barn
analogy.relationship: A source illuminates part of the risk field without proving the rest empty.
correspondence: the beam is the database's coverage
the unlit space is residual uncertainty
analogy.limit: A database has systematic scope and evidence, not a randomly moving beam; the analogy must not imply all sources are equally weak.

concepts.boundary: A limitation does not make the source useless; it defines the claim the source can support.
concepts.misconception: No record means no well, septic problem, contamination, flood exposure or mine hazard.
concepts.expectedAbility: State one supported finding and one residual uncertainty for each source.

retrievals.freshSituation: Post-deed inspection contradicts an estimated well-map point.
retrievals.listenerTask: Explain why the pre-bid record was a clue rather than a false fact.

concepts.name: title versus possession
concepts.durableOutcome: Separate title, encumbrances, easements, occupancy and vacant possession.
concepts.definition: Title describes legal ownership interests; possession describes control or occupancy of the place; each can require a different legal process.
concepts.reason: A tax deed does not safely answer who is inside, whether a tenancy exists or how possession changes.
concepts.mechanism: The deed and title opinion address conveyed interests; occupancy facts and applicable tenancy/possession law determine lawful next steps.
concepts.concreteCase: A deeded four-unit-or-less building remains occupied and the municipality supplies neither keys nor eviction.
concepts.problemBeforeName: The bidder assumes ownership paperwork physically empties the premises.

analogy.name: name on the coat-check ticket versus coat in hand
analogy.relationship: Documented entitlement and physical control are distinct.
correspondence: the ticket resembles evidence of legal entitlement
having the coat resembles actual possession
analogy.limit: Real-property possession and tenancy rights are far more complex, and self-help cannot be inferred from the analogy.

concepts.boundary: The book will not prescribe eviction, lockout or abandoned-goods steps for a specific property.
concepts.misconception: Immediate deed means immediate vacant possession.
concepts.expectedAbility: Ask separate lawyer-reviewed questions about deed, burdens, occupants and possession process.

retrievals.freshSituation: Rent arrives during the redemption period while an occupant remains.
retrievals.listenerTask: Identify why certificate powers do not justify improvising possession actions.

concepts.name: all-in cost
concepts.durableOutcome: Construct an all-in uncertainty budget and written maximum-bid rule without treating the minimum as value.
concepts.definition: The total exposure required to reach a defined use, including bid, taxes, professional work, carrying, condition, possession and uncertainty reserves.
concepts.reason: The auction price is only one cost and the minimum has no built-in allowance for defects or plans.
concepts.mechanism: Start from a defined use and conservative value boundary, subtract known costs and reserves, then set a written maximum that cannot rise in the room.
concepts.concreteCase: A low-minimum building requires HST/tax review, legal work, insurance, security, remediation and occupancy reserves before any rehabilitation budget.
concepts.problemBeforeName: The listener sees a four-figure minimum and compares it directly with ordinary house prices.

analogy.name: iceberg cost stack
analogy.relationship: The visible bid can be smaller than less visible acquisition and responsibility costs.
correspondence: the visible tip is the winning bid
submerged mass is taxes, professional work, carrying, repair and uncertainty
analogy.limit: The proportions are not fixed and known costs should be estimated rather than treated as unknowable danger.

concepts.boundary: The framework is educational and does not select a return target or personalized bid.
concepts.misconception: A winning bid below assessed value is necessarily a bargain.
concepts.expectedAbility: Name the cost categories and derive a stopping number from evidence rather than competition.

retrievals.freshSituation: The live bid crosses the written ceiling by one increment.
retrievals.listenerTask: Decide whether any auction-room fact justifies a higher number.
retrievals.answerPlacement: The fictional bidder lowers the card; the researcher does not change the evidence file.

concepts.name: payment performance
concepts.durableOutcome: Execute registration, immediate payment and any three-business-day balance without confusing the leading bid with a completed sale.
concepts.definition: The bidder's ability to satisfy immediate deposit, accepted-funds and three-business-day balance rules exactly.
concepts.reason: An unaffordable or unavailable payment method voids the apparent win and can create resale costs.
concepts.mechanism: Current event terms are checked, funds and bidder authority are arranged per parcel, and the balance path is rehearsed before bidding.
concepts.concreteCase: An Inverness bidder has the recovery amount and $200 registration amount ready immediately and the verified balance available within three business days.
concepts.problemBeforeName: The listener plans to arrange financing after learning the winning price.

analogy.name: finish line beyond the hammer
analogy.relationship: The high bid is an intermediate event, not completed performance.
correspondence: the hammer identifies the leading bid
accepted payment completes the sale step
analogy.limit: Legal completion includes certificate/deed stages and cannot be reduced to a race.

concepts.boundary: Accepted methods and fees are municipality- and event-specific.
concepts.misconception: Winning creates time to seek an ordinary conditional mortgage approval.
concepts.expectedAbility: State the immediate and three-day obligations and verify event-specific payment readiness.

retrievals.freshSituation: A researched parcel is affordable but the bidder cannot satisfy the event's payment method.
retrievals.listenerTask: Classify it as not ready rather than changing the process after the bid.

concepts.name: staged responsibility
concepts.durableOutcome: Translate auction, tender, minimum bid, immediate deed, redemption, certificate of sale and tax deed into consequences.
concepts.definition: The changing set of rights and duties attached to bidder, paid purchaser, certificate holder and deeded owner states.
concepts.reason: Each stage permits different actions and demands different records, insurance and professional work.
concepts.mechanism: Payment leads to certificate; certificate creates limited protection/use duties; redemption ends rights or expiry permits deed; deed opens possession and ordinary ownership work.
concepts.concreteCase: One building requires insurance during redemption, is not redeemed, then undergoes lawful possession and post-deed inspection.
concepts.problemBeforeName: The listener has one word—owner—for several legally different moments.

analogy.name: relay baton
analogy.relationship: Responsibility changes form at documented handoffs.
correspondence: certificate and deed are handoff documents
each stage carries a different permitted job
analogy.limit: The same purchaser may hold every stage, and legal rights are not literally passed between different runners.

concepts.boundary: Staged responsibility does not guarantee the ability to insure, finance, occupy or develop.
concepts.misconception: The auction win, certificate and deed are interchangeable proof of full ownership.
concepts.expectedAbility: Identify the current stage, document, permitted action and next terminating event.

retrievals.freshSituation: The six months expire without redemption.
retrievals.listenerTask: Name the document to request and the owner questions that remain open.
